Earlier API evidence and costs remain separate. Assessed uncertain hypotheses remain unpublished; completion does not establish equivalence or exhaustive discovery.
The displayed API cost covers the earlier run. Codex subscription and credit usage for this follow-up are recorded separately.

For Regulation 261/2004 the English closing Commission Statement is preserved as interpretive context. It is not a regulation provision and has no counterpart in several supplied language expressions. Its non-parallel presence alone is not an omission of comparable regulation text or a reason to reject coverage. Review every supplied article, recital, footnote and other comparable text. Never infer a translation discrepancy from an absent statement. Record any genuine missing operative source or unresolved legal mechanism. This explicit scope clarification is new to this follow-up; prior evidence remains unchanged.
English provides navigation; all official language versions are equally authoritative. Findings are potential discrepancies reviewed by agents, not adjudicated legal errors.

impact_families.title: Judicial-redress recital expressly mentions compensation claims only
impact_families.effect: In interpreting supervision alongside judicial enforcement of care, the Polish recital offers less explicit support for preserving non-monetary proceedings.
impact_families.rationale: The supported consequence concerns interpretive guidance. The recital does not withdraw jurisdiction or remedies, and the operative enforcement provisions remain.
impact_families.uncertainty: National procedures and contextual interpretation may provide identical judicial protection.

impact_families.title: Portuguese reporting topic addresses effects rather than incidence
impact_families.effect: A Commission report assessing effects on denied boarding and cancellations without addressing their incidence could satisfy the Portuguese topic while omitting the specific English reporting subject.
impact_families.rationale: The change concerns an institutional reporting topic and does not itself alter passenger entitlements, carrier assistance duties or sanctions.
impact_families.uncertainty: An effects assessment may include incidence, and contextual interpretation could require both.

impact_families.title: Services wording may restrict volunteer arrangements and statutory assistance
impact_families.effect: A passenger surrendering a reservation for cash alone could fail to qualify as a volunteer and lose the statutory Article 8 assistance attached to that status.
impact_families.rationale: The restriction reaches an operative definition and eligibility for important reimbursement or replacement-transport rights.
impact_families.uncertainty: Services could be interpreted contextually to encompass all negotiated benefits.

impact_families.title: Full compensation may remain payable at exactly four hours
impact_families.effect: An otherwise compensable residual-category flight arrives exactly four hours late after re-routing. The restrictive Latvian reading could require EUR 600 instead of permitting EUR 300.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed boundary determines whether the carrier may withhold half of the principal fixed compensation entitlement under Article 7.
impact_families.uncertainty: The parallel thresholds support an inclusive four-hour ceiling; the added words leave the boundary ambiguous.

impact_families.title: Voucher payment requires written rather than expressly signed consent
impact_families.effect: A passenger expressly accepts vouchers in an unsigned written message. Croatian could permit that payment without obtaining the signature expressly required by English.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of affirmative consent. It does not authorize unilateral vouchers or change the amount payable.
impact_families.uncertainty: Rules governing written consent or electronic signatures could reconcile the requirements.

impact_families.title: Waiting-time care may exclude refreshments
impact_families.effect: During a qualifying wait, a carrier could provide sufficient food but decline complimentary drinks.
impact_families.rationale: The identified change concerns one component of care. The sources establish no further loss of compensation, transport, accommodation or food entitlements.
impact_families.uncertainty: Sufficient food may contextually include accompanying refreshments.

impact_families.title: Czech cancellation rerouting reverses departure limits and includes arrival boundaries
impact_families.effect: With fifteen days’ notice and rerouting departing thirty minutes early, the Czech list could require compensation despite the English timely-notice exception.
impact_families.rationale: The reversed departure limits can activate Czech points (ii)–(iii), changing the Article 7 compensation remedy. Arrival-boundary effects additionally depend on interpretation of the notice list.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 12 supports harmonization; Czech point (i) independently masks timing effects after short notice.

impact_families.title: Negative notice conditions may preserve cancellation compensation
impact_families.effect: Absent extraordinary circumstances, a passenger given ten days’ notice and qualifying rerouting could retain Article 7 compensation because two-week notice was absent.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed structure determines entitlement to the core cancellation compensation remedy.
impact_families.uncertainty: Reading each limb within its intended notice period could harmonize the provisions.

impact_families.title: Compensation distance may use a destination other than the last delayed destination
impact_families.effect: On connecting travel with several delayed arrivals, choosing an intermediate destination could produce a lower compensation band than choosing the last delayed destination.
impact_families.rationale: The selected endpoint can determine whether the passenger receives EUR 250, EUR 400 or EUR 600.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 2(h) and the journey context strongly support using the last relevant endpoint.

impact_families.title: Volunteer status may require an invitation addressed to all passengers
impact_families.effect: A passenger surrendering a reservation after a selective invitation could lose the statutory Article 8 choice of reimbursement or rerouting if the Croatian audience requirement controlled.
impact_families.rationale: Article 4(1) makes that important travel remedy additional to negotiated benefits and attaches it to volunteer status.
impact_families.uncertainty: A general-call understanding of English or protective interpretation of Croatian could reconcile the outcomes.

impact_families.title: Cancellation accommodation may require a full elapsed day
impact_families.effect: A passenger outside Article 11’s protected groups needs accommodation between a cancelled 22:00 flight and an 08:00 replacement. An elapsed-day reading could exclude hotel and transfer assistance.
impact_families.rationale: The reading could remove an important overnight-care entitlement despite a necessary stay. Article 9 does not independently override the trigger.
impact_families.uncertainty: A next-calendar-day interpretation could reconcile the wording.

impact_families.title: French redress safeguard can extend to third parties without a carrier contract
impact_families.effect: A non-contracting third party could invoke the French safeguard against an interpretation that the Regulation restricts an independently existing right of redress.
impact_families.rationale: The change extends a non-restriction safeguard. It does not create a cause of action, establish liability or determine recovery.
impact_families.uncertainty: The preceding contractual-redress provision supports harmonization; no underlying claim is established.

impact_families.title: Spanish short-notice cancellation exception expressly requires another flight
impact_families.effect: Timely comparable rail rerouting after short-notice cancellation could satisfy the English compensation exception while failing the Spanish requirement to offer another flight.
impact_families.rationale: The transport-mode condition can determine whether fixed cancellation compensation remains payable in full or is excluded.
impact_families.uncertainty: The aviation context could support a flight-only interpretation of English rerouting in this exception.

impact_families.title: Cancellation arrival limits include exactly two or four hours
impact_families.effect: With ten days’ notice and otherwise qualifying rerouting arriving exactly four hours late, the inclusive limit could exclude compensation if the surrounding provision operates as a notice exception.
impact_families.rationale: The boundary can determine the entire cancellation compensation entitlement. Its narrow timing range does not reduce that conditional consequence.
impact_families.uncertainty: The outcome depends on resolving the separate Slovak negative-condition structure.

impact_families.title: Danish operating-carrier definition omits the express licence link
impact_families.effect: An unlicensed undertaking operating an otherwise covered departure from a Member State could bear compensation and assistance duties under the Danish definition but fall outside the English licence-linked definition.
impact_families.rationale: The definition controls the persons bearing the Regulation’s principal compensation and assistance obligations.
impact_families.uncertainty: The compound defined name and Article 2(a) support implicitly requiring licensed-carrier status.

impact_families.title: Voucher payment may require written rather than signed agreement
impact_families.effect: A passenger's genuine unsigned written acceptance could authorize payment in vouchers without a signature.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of affirmative consent, including incorporated reimbursement payments. It does not authorize unwanted vouchers or reduce the amount due.
impact_families.uncertainty: Interpretation of written agreement could require equivalent authentication.

impact_families.title: Portuguese voucher compensation requires written rather than expressly signed agreement
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely accepting vouchers in an unsigned written message could authorize that payment method under Portuguese while English requires a signed agreement.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of genuine agreement. It does not remove consent, reduce compensation or permit unilateral voucher payment.
impact_families.uncertainty: Rules interpreting written agreement and electronic signatures could harmonize the formalities.

impact_families.title: Lithuanian residual compensation category lacks an amount
impact_families.effect: For an otherwise compensable denied boarding in the residual flight category, the Lithuanian provision supplies no fixed amount where English specifies EUR 600.
impact_families.rationale: The omission concerns the entire amount of a principal compensation entitlement, rather than its payment procedure.
impact_families.uncertainty: Multilingual interpretation could supply EUR 600; the omission does not establish a zero entitlement.

impact_families.title: Check-in eligibility may depend on instructions in the ticket
impact_families.effect: A passenger meets the 45-minute fallback but misses an earlier deadline communicated separately from the ticket. A ticket-only reading could preserve eligibility that the English wording excludes.
impact_families.rationale: Article 3(2) controls access to compensation and assistance, subject to its cancellation and transfer qualifications.
impact_families.uncertainty: Associated written instructions might be treated as incorporated into an electronic ticket.

impact_families.title: Delay accommodation trigger may require an elapsed full day
impact_families.effect: A passenger outside Article 11’s protected groups faces a qualifying overnight delay shorter than 24 hours. An elapsed-day reading could exclude necessary hotel accommodation and transfers.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed condition controls an important overnight-care entitlement; Article 9 does not independently replace the Article 6 trigger.
impact_families.uncertainty: The Croatian expression also permits a next-calendar-day interpretation.

impact_families.title: Bulgarian compensation defence refers to necessary rather than reasonable measures
impact_families.effect: A necessary but unreasonable avoidance measure could defeat the Bulgarian compensation defence, although failure to take that measure would not defeat the English reasonable-measures test.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed standard controls the carrier’s exemption from Article 7 compensation and therefore an important passenger remedy and corresponding payment duty.
impact_families.uncertainty: Bulgarian recital 14 supports interpreting necessary measures as reasonably necessary.

impact_families.title: The short-notice cancellation exception may reverse the departure boundary
impact_families.effect: With cancellation notified less than seven days ahead, a replacement departing three hours early and arriving on time could satisfy only the Romanian compensation exception.
impact_families.rationale: The boundary can determine entitlement to Article 7 compensation, subject to that article's amounts and reduction provisions.
impact_families.uncertainty: The adjacent exception and passenger-protection context support harmonization.

impact_families.title: Finnish changes compensation brackets at exactly 3500 kilometres
impact_families.effect: For an eligible non-intra-Community flight of exactly 3500 kilometres with no applicable reduction, the compensation could be EUR 600 under Finnish instead of EUR 400.
impact_families.rationale: The endpoint changes the principal monetary remedy by EUR 200 and also changes the timing condition for halving it.
impact_families.uncertainty: English's interval is less explicit about its endpoint; harmonized interpretation may resolve the difference.

impact_families.title: Care-specific wording may narrow the third-country exclusion
impact_families.effect: An otherwise qualifying passenger arriving on a Community carrier received compensation and re-routing abroad but no care. The disputed reading determines whether the Regulation remains applicable.
impact_families.rationale: The exclusion controls access to the Regulation's core compensation, reimbursement, re-routing and care rights.
impact_families.uncertainty: Assistance could contextually mean care in this exclusion.

impact_families.title: Czech agreed airport-transfer destinations lack an express proximity limit
impact_families.effect: Following arrival at an alternative airport, a more distant agreed destination could fall within the Czech statutory transfer-cost duty.
impact_families.rationale: The change concerns an ancillary transfer expense conditioned on agreement. Substantial financial exposure is not established.
impact_families.uncertainty: The surrounding geographical context may imply proximity.

impact_families.title: Finnish postpones the care threshold at exactly 3500 kilometres
impact_families.effect: For a passenger outside Article 11's protected categories, a predicted three-and-a-half-hour delay on a non-intra-Community flight of exactly 3500 kilometres could leave care temporarily unavailable under Finnish.
impact_families.rationale: The identified change postpones care by one hour at a distance boundary; it does not change the separate five-hour reimbursement rule.
impact_families.uncertainty: The English endpoint and harmonized interpretation remain open.

impact_families.title: Hungarian operating-carrier definition requires a contractual link to the passenger's counterparty
impact_families.effect: A carrier operates on behalf of the passenger's counterparty through an intermediary, without contracting directly with that counterparty, and invokes the Hungarian definition to resist operating-carrier duties.
impact_families.rationale: Operating-carrier status determines responsibility for core compensation and assistance obligations.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 7, Article 3(5) and a broader understanding of the contractual relationship support harmonization.

impact_families.title: Lithuanian changes the boundaries for halving compensation
impact_families.effect: After compensable denied boarding on a flight of 1500 kilometres or less, an alternative arriving exactly two hours late could require EUR 250 under Lithuanian instead of permitting EUR 125.
impact_families.rationale: The boundary determines whether half of the principal fixed compensation entitlement can be withheld.
impact_families.uncertainty: Contextual interpretation could harmonize the boundaries, especially for on-time or earlier arrivals.

impact_families.title: Voucher consent may not expressly require a signature
impact_families.effect: A carrier could accept unsigned written consent to voucher payment where English expressly requires a signature.
impact_families.rationale: This changes an authentication safeguard. Affirmative written consent remains necessary, and ordinary monetary payment remains available.
impact_families.uncertainty: Applicable formal rules could treat written consent as necessarily signed.

impact_families.title: Written consent may permit vouchers without a signature
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely accepts vouchers in an unsigned written message. The Polish reading could validate that payment while the English wording requires a signature.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of affirmative consent, including incorporated reimbursement payments. It does not authorize compulsory vouchers or remove the underlying payment entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Applicable written-form requirements could themselves require a signature.

impact_families.title: Volunteer solicitation may depend on a planned boarding refusal
impact_families.effect: A carrier anticipates insufficient capacity but has not planned a boarding refusal. The Latvian reading could postpone its call for volunteers.
impact_families.rationale: The identified consequence concerns procedural timing. Article 4(2) still requires insufficient volunteers before involuntary denial, and Article 4(3) preserves compensation and assistance.
impact_families.uncertainty: Planning could be interpreted to include reasonable anticipation.

impact_families.title: Written consent may replace signed agreement for voucher payment
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely accepts a voucher in unsigned writing. Slovenian could permit that payment, whereas the English signature condition would remain unsatisfied.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of consent, including for payments incorporating Article 7(3). It does not remove consent or change the amount owed.
impact_families.uncertainty: Applicable formal requirements might equate written consent with signed agreement.

impact_families.title: Priority carriage specifies guide dogs without express certification
impact_families.effect: When limited capacity makes priority decisive, a certified non-guide assistance dog could lose priority to accompany a passenger with reduced mobility.
impact_families.rationale: The wording changes eligibility for an express disability-related transport entitlement. Priority for the passenger does not independently secure priority for the accompanying dog.
impact_families.uncertainty: Guide dogs might receive a broader contextual meaning; certification might be implicit.

impact_families.title: Greek earliest-rerouting right expressly requires a flight
impact_families.effect: Where comparable rail transport offers earlier onward travel than any flight, the Greek reading could permit the carrier to withhold that option and provide a later flight.
impact_families.rationale: The difference can narrow the substantive right to onward transport at the earliest opportunity, a principal alternative to reimbursement.
impact_families.uncertainty: The aviation context could support interpreting English rerouting as flight-only.

impact_families.title: Danish cancellation exception may also remove the confirmed-reservation condition
impact_families.effect: An otherwise qualifying passenger without a confirmed reservation, and without a transfer under Article 3(2)(b), could obtain cancellation rights through the broader Danish exception.
impact_families.rationale: Removing the confirmed-reservation requirement changes threshold eligibility for compensation and assistance under the Regulation.
impact_families.uncertainty: Passenger status remains necessary; context may confine the Danish exception to check-in.

impact_families.title: Hungarian voucher-payment condition specifies written consent
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely accepts vouchers in an unsigned written message, which the carrier treats as sufficient consent under Hungarian.
impact_families.rationale: The supported change concerns the form of consent to an agreed payment method, without reducing compensation or dispensing with agreement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Applicable rules on written consent and electronic signatures may align the outcomes.

impact_families.title: Dutch compensation-reduction limits can also count early arrival
impact_families.effect: Where compensation is otherwise due for a flight of 1500 kilometres or less, an alternative arriving over two hours early could preserve EUR 250 under Dutch instead of permitting EUR 125.
impact_families.rationale: The direction of the timing test controls whether half of the fixed compensation entitlement may be withheld.
impact_families.uncertainty: Contextual interpretation could confine the Dutch deviation test to late arrival.

impact_families.title: Compensation amounts may operate as ceilings
impact_families.effect: A qualifying short-flight passenger could receive less than EUR 250 despite the absence of conditions permitting the express reduction.
impact_families.rationale: Treating the fixed compensation amounts as discretionary ceilings could materially reduce the principal monetary entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Articles 7(2) and 15 strongly support interpreting the amounts as fixed.

impact_families.title: Services wording may narrow the third-country exclusion
impact_families.effect: An otherwise eligible passenger receives assistance and a non-compensatory gift of goods qualifying as a benefit. Slovenian could preserve protection that the English exclusion removes.
impact_families.rationale: The exception controls access to the Regulation's compensation, reimbursement, rerouting and care rights for the covered third-country journey.
impact_families.uncertainty: The advantage must qualify as a benefit; compensation or a broad reading of services could eliminate the difference.

impact_families.title: Spanish compensation reduction can extend to alternative non-air transport
impact_families.effect: Following involuntary denied boarding, comparable rail rerouting arriving within the relevant limit could permit a Spanish 50% compensation reduction, while English expressly requires an alternative flight.
impact_families.rationale: The broader transport condition can remove half of an otherwise payable statutory compensation remedy.
impact_families.uncertainty: The aviation context could support interpreting alternative transport as an alternative flight.

impact_families.title: Passenger eligibility omits an express alternative
impact_families.effect: A passenger with a confirmed reservation and timely check-in could be denied protection solely because no transfer to another flight occurred.
impact_families.rationale: Article 3 controls eligibility for the Regulation's principal compensation and assistance rights.
impact_families.uncertainty: The separate situations and protective scheme strongly support alternative eligibility routes.

impact_families.title: Hungarian service-dog priority expressly covers two assistance categories
impact_families.effect: A certified hearing-assistance dog accompanying an eligible passenger could fall outside the express Hungarian priority categories.
impact_families.rationale: The identified consequence concerns the dog's express carriage priority. The provision does not establish a carriage prohibition or remove the passenger's priority.
impact_families.uncertainty: The inclusive disability definition supports a broader interpretation of the named dog categories.

impact_families.title: Greek dog-carriage priority changes category and certification conditions
impact_families.effect: A certified non-guide service dog could lose express priority, while an uncertified guide dog could gain priority under Greek.
impact_families.rationale: The demonstrated change concerns preferential carriage for accompanying dogs. Passenger priority remains, and neither version determines ordinary dog-admission rights through this provision.
impact_families.uncertainty: Context could broaden guide dogs or imply qualification; the supplied text does not expressly resolve either issue.

impact_families.title: Dutch cancellation-compensation exceptions require another flight
impact_families.effect: After cancellation notified less than seven days beforehand, suitable rail re-routing meeting both timing limits could remove compensation under the broader English reading but leave it payable under Dutch.
impact_families.rationale: The transport-mode condition can determine entitlement to the full Article 7 compensation amount, absent another exemption.
impact_families.uncertainty: Contextual interpretation could give re-routing and another flight the same scope for these exceptions.

impact_families.title: Bulgarian replacement-flight departure limits run in the opposite direction
impact_families.effect: With cancellation notified three days beforehand, replacement transport departing three hours early and arriving on time could exclude compensation under Bulgarian but fail the English exception.
impact_families.rationale: The reversed departure limit can determine eligibility for the Article 7 compensation entitlement, assuming the other conditions hold and no independent exemption applies.
impact_families.uncertainty: The protective purpose supports harmonization, but the Bulgarian temporal direction is explicit.

impact_families.title: German cancellation exceptions include exact arrival-time limits
impact_families.effect: Otherwise qualifying replacement transport arriving exactly two hours late after cancellation notified fewer than seven days beforehand could exclude German compensation while leaving English compensation payable.
impact_families.rationale: The difference can eliminate a statutory monetary remedy. Any Article 7(2) reduction still leaves a payment under the English reading.
impact_families.uncertainty: The scenario assumes other eligibility conditions hold and no independent exemption applies; contextual harmonization remains possible.

impact_families.title: Portuguese carriage priority expressly covers certified guide dogs
impact_families.effect: Where limited capacity makes priority decisive, a certified non-guiding service dog accompanying a person with reduced mobility could lose priority under Portuguese.
impact_families.rationale: The narrower category materially reduces the express disability-related carriage priority for an accompanying assistance animal.
impact_families.uncertainty: Guide dogs could receive a broader contextual interpretation; the passenger's own priority remains.

impact_families.title: Carrier wording may broaden responsibility for passenger remedies
impact_families.effect: A non-operating contracting carrier placing a passenger in a lower class could become liable for Article 10 reimbursement under the broader Croatian wording.
impact_families.rationale: The reading changes the potential bearer of a core remedy, including reimbursement of up to 75% of the ticket price.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 7 and the operational context strongly support limiting responsibility to the operating carrier.

impact_families.title: Czech third-country condition can exclude passengers receiving only one form of support
impact_families.effect: An otherwise eligible inbound passenger receives meals but no benefits or compensation abroad. The Czech reading could exclude the passenger from the Regulation.
impact_families.rationale: The condition controls access to compensation, reimbursement, rerouting and care as a whole.
impact_families.uncertainty: Contextual interpretation could reconcile the Czech negatives with a combined exclusion.

impact_families.title: Hungarian Gibraltar notification does not expressly require a commencement date
impact_families.effect: The governments notify the Council that the arrangements apply but omit the commencement date.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the required information in a notification. Both versions independently link the suspension's end to implementation of the arrangements.
impact_families.uncertainty: The suspension context may imply that the notification must identify the commencement date.

impact_families.title: Delay accommodation may require 24 elapsed hours
impact_families.effect: An otherwise qualifying evening flight delayed until the next morning could fail the accommodation condition because fewer than 24 hours separate the departure times.
impact_families.rationale: Necessary overnight accommodation and transfers could be excluded for passengers outside Article 11's independent protection.
impact_families.uncertainty: The necessary-stay provisions and protective purpose support calendar-day harmonization.

impact_families.title: Czech mandatory check-in notice omits cancellation
impact_families.effect: A carrier using the prescribed Czech display could satisfy its wording without mentioning cancellation.
impact_families.rationale: The difference narrows a general information duty. Individual cancellation notices and substantive passenger entitlements remain required.
impact_families.uncertainty: The practical effect depends partly on compliance with the individual-notice duty.

impact_families.title: Czech overnight-delay provision references meals instead of hotel accommodation
impact_families.effect: A passenger outside Article 11 needs accommodation during a delay meeting both versions’ timing conditions. Czech could require meals and transfers without requiring a hotel.
impact_families.rationale: The cross-reference can remove necessary overnight accommodation, an important care entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: The repeated meals reference and retained accommodation transport strongly support contextual correction.

impact_families.title: Portuguese triggers delay reimbursement after four hours
impact_families.effect: At four hours of delay but before five hours, a qualifying passenger could choose reimbursement and any applicable return flight under Portuguese before the English trigger is reached.
impact_families.rationale: The threshold determines access to the principal remedy allowing passengers to abandon travel and recover qualifying ticket costs.
impact_families.uncertainty: Multilingual interpretation could reconcile the threshold; Article 8's substantive conditions and package-travel qualification remain.

impact_families.title: Dutch voucher compensation requires written rather than expressly signed consent
impact_families.effect: A passenger's genuine acceptance of vouchers in an unsigned written message could authorize that payment method under Dutch while requiring a signature under English.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of consent. It neither removes consent nor changes the compensation amount or permits unilateral substitution.
impact_families.uncertainty: Interpretation of written consent and electronic signatures could eliminate the distinction.

impact_families.title: Bulgarian reporting deadline excludes 1 January 2007
impact_families.effect: A report made on 1 January 2007 could satisfy the English deadline but be late under Bulgarian.
impact_families.rationale: The supported consequence is a one-day boundary for an institutional reporting duty. No resulting change to passenger remedies or carrier obligations is specified.
impact_families.uncertainty: Deadline-calculation rules not supplied here might reconcile the practical deadline.

impact_families.title: Danish cancellation exceptions include exact arrival-time limits
impact_families.effect: Following cancellation notified fewer than seven days beforehand, otherwise qualifying rerouting arriving exactly two hours late could exclude compensation under Danish but not English.
impact_families.rationale: The boundary can eliminate the statutory compensation remedy. Article 7(2)’s possible reduction does not preserve a payment when the cancellation exception applies.
impact_families.uncertainty: Other eligibility conditions and independent exemptions remain; multilingual interpretation could reconcile the boundary.

impact_families.title: Opposite departure limits in a cancellation compensation exception
impact_families.effect: With ten days' notice, a replacement departs three hours early and arrives on time. Polish could exempt the carrier from compensation while the English departure condition would not.
impact_families.rationale: The reversed condition can determine the passenger's entire Article 7 cancellation-compensation entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Context supports harmonization; independent compensation exemptions remain applicable.

impact_families.title: Danish delay-accommodation trigger sets an upper time limit
impact_families.effect: For a passenger outside Article 11, departure expected two days late could fail the Danish accommodation trigger despite requiring overnight stays, while satisfying English.
impact_families.rationale: The reversed limit could remove necessary hotel accommodation and transfers during a multi-day delay. Meals and the reimbursement option do not preserve this care entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 6(2), Article 9 and the protective purpose support a harmonizing interpretation.

impact_families.title: Airport-transfer costs may fall on a non-operating carrier
impact_families.effect: A non-operating carrier arranging travel and offering arrival at another airport could have to pay the passenger's transfer to the booked airport or agreed nearby destination.
impact_families.rationale: The concrete extension concerns an ancillary transfer expense; principal compensation and assistance duties expressly retain operating-carrier responsibility.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 7 and surrounding operator-specific duties support a narrower interpretation.

impact_families.title: Portuguese cancellation exceptions include the exact arrival-time limits
impact_families.effect: After cancellation notified less than seven days beforehand, otherwise compliant re-routing arriving exactly two hours late could eliminate compensation under Portuguese but preserve entitlement under English.
impact_families.rationale: The inclusive boundary can remove the full cancellation-compensation entitlement, subject to the remaining conditions and independent exemptions.
impact_families.uncertainty: Multilingual interpretation could harmonize the limits; extraordinary circumstances may independently exclude compensation.

impact_families.title: Italian cancellation-care wording can require a full day's postponement
impact_families.effect: After cancellation of a 22:00 flight, a passenger outside Article 11's protected categories needs accommodation before an 08:00 replacement. A full-day reading could exclude hotel and transfer assistance.
impact_families.rationale: The elapsed-day condition could remove an important overnight-care entitlement despite accommodation being necessary.
impact_families.uncertainty: A calendar-day interpretation and the protective context could harmonize the texts.

impact_families.title: Greek compensation-distance instruction omits cancellation
impact_families.effect: For a cancellation affecting connecting travel, the restrictive Greek reading leaves the applicable distance basis unresolved.
impact_families.rationale: Article 7 sets monetary distance bands, but the omission supplies no replacement measurement rule. A lower compensation band cannot be established merely by assuming the omission applies.
impact_families.uncertainty: Articles 5 and 2(h) support harmonization; the alternative calculation and resulting amount remain unresolved.

impact_families.title: Swedish makes completed check-in an eligibility condition
impact_families.effect: An otherwise eligible passenger presents on time but the carrier leaves check-in unfinished and denies boarding. If Article 3(2)(b) does not apply, Swedish could exclude compensation and assistance that English preserves.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed requirement controls access to substantive passenger protections, including Article 4 compensation and assistance, rather than merely prescribing an administrative procedure.
impact_families.uncertainty: A functional reading of completed check-in, supported by the protective purpose, could reconcile the texts.

impact_families.title: Czech delay wording may postpone accommodation transport until a full day’s delay
impact_families.effect: A qualifying delay from late evening to the next morning could fail the Czech elapsed-day trigger for accommodation transport.
impact_families.rationale: With the supplied Czech cross-references, meals remain independently due and hotels are separately omitted. The isolated timing change affects the ancillary transport duty.
impact_families.uncertainty: A calendar-day reading and Article 6(2) support harmonization; Article 11 separately protects specified passengers.

impact_families.title: Cancellation exceptions include arrival exactly two or four hours late
impact_families.effect: With cancellation notice less than seven days beforehand, compliant replacement departure and arrival exactly two hours late, Polish could exclude compensation while English preserves entitlement, absent another exemption.
impact_families.rationale: The inclusive boundary can eliminate the entire cancellation-compensation entitlement, even where Article 7 would otherwise permit a reduction.
impact_families.uncertainty: Other exception conditions must be met; contextual harmonization remains possible.

impact_families.title: Longer waiting may trigger hotel accommodation without a necessary stay
impact_families.effect: After involuntary denied boarding, a passenger awaiting a same-day replacement flight could claim hotel accommodation despite no necessary additional stay.
impact_families.rationale: Removing the necessity threshold materially expands eligibility for the substantive accommodation entitlement and the carrier's corresponding duty.
impact_families.uncertainty: The hotel-accommodation context may imply that the extended wait must necessitate a stay.

impact_families.title: Dutch re-routing options expressly require another flight
impact_families.effect: If comparable rail transport reaches the final destination before any replacement flight, Dutch could allow the carrier to withhold that option under an air-only reading.
impact_families.rationale: The restriction could materially narrow the principal entitlement to re-routing at the earliest opportunity.
impact_families.uncertainty: The aviation context could support a harmonized interpretation of the available replacement transport.

impact_families.title: Dutch priority carriage expressly covers guide dogs
impact_families.effect: Where limited capacity makes priority decisive, an accompanying certified service dog performing non-guiding assistance could lose priority under the narrower Dutch category.
impact_families.rationale: The difference removes an express disability-related carriage priority for an assistance animal, materially narrowing the accessibility protection in Article 11(1).
impact_families.uncertainty: Guide dogs could receive a broader contextual meaning; the passenger's own priority remains.

impact_families.title: Spanish compensation-reduction limit may also measure early arrival
impact_families.effect: After an otherwise compensable short-haul cancellation, a replacement departing four hours early and arriving three hours early could permit an English 50% reduction but fail an absolute-difference Spanish limit.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed measurement can determine whether the passenger retains half of the fixed compensation otherwise subject to reduction.
impact_families.uncertainty: Spanish difference may be interpreted contextually as lateness only.

impact_families.title: Cancellation accommodation may require a full day's postponement
impact_families.effect: An ordinary passenger's cancelled evening flight is replaced the next morning, less than 24 hours later. The elapsed-day reading could exclude necessary hotel accommodation and associated transport.
impact_families.rationale: The reading could remove the entire overnight-care entitlement under Article 5(1)(b). Article 9 supplies the care conditions; Article 11 separately protects specified passengers with special needs.
impact_families.uncertainty: Latvian Article 6 and Article 9's overnight-stay purpose strongly support a calendar-day interpretation.

impact_families.title: Suitable implementation means may extend beyond passenger information
impact_families.effect: A carrier could have to provide suitable means for a blind passenger to exercise a rerouting choice, beyond accessible notices.
impact_families.rationale: The additional effect concerns implementation methods. Substantive entitlements remain unchanged, and the Regulation already provides adaptation and special-attention protections.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 14's subject may confine the broader reference to information duties.

impact_families.title: Swedish cancellation exceptions include arrival exactly at the time limits
impact_families.effect: With cancellation notice less than seven days beforehand and otherwise compliant re-routing arriving exactly two hours late, Swedish could eliminate Article 7 compensation that English preserves, absent another exemption.
impact_families.rationale: The difference can extinguish the monetary entitlement entirely. Article 7(2) may reduce the English entitlement but does not eliminate it.
impact_families.uncertainty: Multilingual interpretation may reconcile the thresholds; the scenario assumes all other eligibility and exception conditions are satisfied.

impact_families.title: Agreed transfer destinations may be limited to airports
impact_families.effect: After arrival at an alternative airport, transfer to an agreed nearby station could fall outside the Slovak transfer-cost obligation.
impact_families.rationale: The difference narrows an ancillary endpoint option. The carrier must still fund transfer to the originally booked airport.
impact_families.uncertainty: The airport context could support a narrower interpretation of English.

impact_families.title: Completed-travel reimbursement condition lacks the negation
impact_families.effect: A passenger whose disrupted journey has lost its original purpose could be refused reimbursement for completed portions under the affirmative Croatian condition.
impact_families.rationale: The condition directly controls a core reimbursement entitlement. The scenario can arise outside the package-travel reimbursement exception.
impact_families.uncertainty: The remedial scheme and return-flight provision strongly support restoring the negative meaning through interpretation.

impact_families.title: The cancellation defence may require adoption of all possible measures
impact_families.effect: A carrier could lose the cancellation compensation defence because it omitted a possible but unreasonable measure.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed test determines exemption from the principal Article 7 compensation duty.
impact_families.uncertainty: Romanian recitals repeatedly support the reasonable-measures standard.

impact_families.title: German voucher-payment consent lacks an express signature requirement
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely accepts vouchers in an unsigned written message. German could permit that payment method while the express English signature condition remains unmet.
impact_families.rationale: The supported change concerns the form of actual consent. It does not authorize unilateral vouchers or reduce the compensation amount.
impact_families.uncertainty: Written consent may be interpreted as signed consent; electronic-signature treatment could also reconcile the texts.

impact_families.title: Maltese reverses the distance threshold for 50% downgrading reimbursement
impact_families.effect: For a downgraded intra-Community flight above 3500 kilometres outside the overseas-department exception, Maltese could require reimbursement of 75% instead of 50% of the ticket price.
impact_families.rationale: The residual bracket establishes a concrete change of 25 percentage points in the statutory reimbursement remedy.
impact_families.uncertainty: The overlapping short-distance brackets and thresholds elsewhere strongly support a harmonizing interpretation.

impact_families.title: Denied-boarding protection may arise before presentation for boarding
impact_families.effect: A checked-in passenger is refused carriage before presenting for boarding and obtains Article 4(3) compensation and assistance under the Slovenian reading.
impact_families.rationale: The definition controls eligibility for mandatory compensation, reimbursement or rerouting, and care.
impact_families.uncertainty: Presentation could be understood as check-in, or actual presentation could be implicit in the Slovenian context.

impact_families.title: Alternative means may extend beyond passenger information
impact_families.effect: A carrier could have to provide an alternative means for a blind passenger to communicate a reimbursement choice, beyond providing accessible information.
impact_families.rationale: The supported change concerns implementation of existing rights; it does not change compensation amounts, transport choices or eligibility.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 14's information context may confine the broader reference.

impact_families.title: Prior assistance alone may exclude incoming passengers
impact_families.effect: An otherwise eligible incoming passenger who received assistance alone could lose access to compensation, reimbursement, rerouting and care under the Estonian reading.
impact_families.rationale: The condition controls eligibility for the Regulation as a whole, including its principal passenger entitlements.
impact_families.uncertainty: The protective purpose supports harmonization of the differently structured conditions.

impact_families.title: Qualifying rerouting may preserve cancellation compensation
impact_families.effect: Notice five days before departure with rerouting arriving one hour late could preserve compensation under Estonian despite satisfying the English exception.
impact_families.rationale: The wording changes a central compensation entitlement and payment duty, subject to the extraordinary-circumstances defence and any applicable reduction.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 12 strongly supports interpreting qualifying notice and rerouting as exceptions.

impact_families.title: Danish dog-carriage priority specifies guide dogs
impact_families.effect: A certified non-guide service dog accompanying an eligible passenger could lack express carriage priority under Danish while receiving it under English.
impact_families.rationale: The supported consequence is the dog’s preferential carriage. Passenger priority and care remain; an inability to travel or a prohibition on carrying the dog is not established.
impact_families.uncertainty: An inclusive interpretation of guide dog could reconcile the texts.

impact_families.title: Bulgarian immediate-care provision omits the express Article 9 entitlement
impact_families.effect: During a delay below Article 6 thresholds, an unaccompanied child could receive unspecified special assistance without the applicable free meals and communications expressly secured by English Article 11(2).
impact_families.rationale: The missing reference could narrow the substantive immediate-care entitlement for expressly protected passengers. Article 9(3) does not independently activate the care package.
impact_families.uncertainty: Shared care terminology, Article 9(3) and the protective purpose support incorporating Article 9 contextually.

impact_families.title: Denied-boarding exclusions may be limited to listed grounds
impact_families.effect: An otherwise eligible passenger refused boarding on a reasonable ground outside the listed subjects could retain Article 4 compensation and assistance under the narrower exclusion.
impact_families.rationale: The definition controls access to the core denied-boarding compensation and assistance duties.
impact_families.uncertainty: The list may be harmonized as illustrative; no actual unlisted refusal is established.

impact_families.title: Volunteer rights may arise before presentation for boarding
impact_families.effect: A checked-in passenger accepts a surrender proposal before presenting for boarding and gains volunteer status and Article 8 assistance under Slovenian.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed condition controls access to important reimbursement or replacement-transport rights.
impact_families.uncertainty: English presentation may encompass check-in; Slovenian boarding context may imply actual presentation.

impact_families.title: Maltese may reverse coverage for third-country departures
impact_families.effect: An otherwise eligible passenger arriving from a third country on a Community carrier who received nothing there could fall outside the Regulation under the positive Maltese condition.
impact_families.rationale: Article 3 determines access to the Regulation's principal compensation and assistance entitlements as a whole.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 6 and the protective scheme support interpreting the condition as an exception.

impact_families.title: Alternative compensation names travellers' cheques instead of travel vouchers
impact_families.effect: A passenger and carrier could expressly agree to compensation in travellers' cheques under Estonian where English expressly identifies travel vouchers.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns an agreed payment instrument; it does not remove monetary payment, reduce the amount due or authorize substitution without agreement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Bank cheques, other services and contextual interpretation may accommodate overlapping arrangements.

impact_families.title: Danish voucher-payment consent requires writing without an express signature
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely approves vouchers in an unsigned written message. Danish could permit that payment while the express English signature condition remains unmet.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the form of consent, without reducing compensation or permitting unilateral substitution of vouchers.
impact_families.uncertainty: An implied signature requirement or treatment of electronic signatures could reconcile the conditions.

impact_families.title: The two-hour care threshold may extend to longer flights
impact_families.effect: A passenger on a longer flight could receive meals and communications after two hours instead of the otherwise applicable three or four hours.
impact_families.rationale: The identified consequence advances interim care. Accommodation retains additional conditions, and reimbursement retains its five-hour trigger.
impact_families.uncertainty: The contradictory phrase and neighboring distance brackets strongly support harmonization.

impact_families.title: Free messages may supplement the two free telephone calls
impact_families.effect: A qualifying passenger could request a free fax after using two free telephone calls.
impact_families.rationale: This adds an ancillary communication benefit; the supplied provisions establish no major consequence for compensation, transport or accommodation.
impact_families.uncertainty: Context could support a shared numerical limit; unlimited messaging is not established.

impact_families.title: Greek hotel-care wording may exclude daytime accommodation
impact_families.effect: Following involuntary denied boarding, a necessary additional daytime hotel stay could fall outside the Greek overnight-only reading while qualifying under the English additional-stay alternative.
impact_families.rationale: The identified restriction concerns daytime hotel accommodation. Overnight lodging, rerouting, compensation and other care remain; no broader deprivation is established.
impact_families.uncertainty: The Greek additional-stay alternative supports reading the hotel benefit more broadly.

impact_families.title: Cancellation accommodation may require a full day's postponement
impact_families.effect: A passenger rerouted from an evening cancellation to the next morning could lose necessary overnight accommodation and transfers because fewer than 24 hours elapsed.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed gateway controls substantive overnight care. Article 11's independent protection does not cover every passenger.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 9 and the protective recitals support a calendar-day interpretation.

impact_families.title: French overseas routes may lose the 75% downgrade reimbursement
impact_families.effect: A downgraded passenger on a specified French overseas route outside categories (a) and (b) could lose the expressly provided 75% ticket-price reimbursement.
impact_families.rationale: The exclusion can remove a substantial quantified reimbursement entitlement; the other categories do not supply a rate for the assumed route.
impact_families.uncertainty: The reimbursement duty and category structure strongly support harmonization.

impact_families.title: Italian delay-care wording can require a full day's postponement
impact_families.effect: A qualifying delay moves departure from 22:00 to 08:00 next morning. A passenger outside Article 11's protected categories who needs accommodation could lose hotel and transfer assistance.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed threshold could remove necessary overnight care while the passenger continues the journey; the five-hour reimbursement option does not replace that entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Interpreting one day as a calendar-day change could avoid the divergence.

impact_families.title: Accommodation transport expressly covers only the outward journey
impact_families.effect: A passenger receives accommodation and transport there but must arrange and pay for the return journey to the airport.
impact_families.rationale: The supported consequence concerns one ancillary ground transfer. Accommodation, re-routing and other care entitlements remain; the supplied text establishes no larger consequence.
impact_families.uncertainty: The purpose of accommodation pending departure could support an implied return-transfer duty.

impact_families.title: Cancellation accommodation may require a full elapsed day
impact_families.effect: After an evening cancellation, a passenger rerouted the next morning could lose necessary accommodation and transfers if 24 elapsed hours were required and Article 11 did not separately protect them.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed trigger could eliminate the overnight-care entitlement, rather than merely alter its administration.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 9 and the care recitals strongly support a calendar-day interpretation.

impact_families.title: Cancellation compensation exceptions may include exact arrival-delay limits
impact_families.effect: A passenger notified three days before departure receives rerouting arriving exactly two hours late. The Croatian endpoint reading could exclude compensation otherwise payable under the English wording.
impact_families.rationale: The difference concerns the existence of a compensation entitlement, including any reduced amount remaining payable under Article 7.
impact_families.uncertainty: The Croatian expressions may instead receive an exclusive, harmonized interpretation.

impact_families.title: Greek prompt special-needs care depends on delay seriousness
impact_families.effect: During a delay below Article 6 thresholds, an eligible passenger could lose prompt Article 9 care if the carrier treats the delay as insufficiently serious under Greek.
impact_families.rationale: The added condition can remove an important immediate-care entitlement specifically granted to passengers with reduced mobility, their companions and unaccompanied children.
impact_families.uncertainty: Seriousness is undefined; protective contextual interpretation may preserve care during short delays.

impact_families.title: The duty to seek volunteers may extend to non-operating carriers
impact_families.effect: A non-operating carrier anticipating denied boarding could itself become obliged to seek volunteers before passengers are refused carriage.
impact_families.rationale: This extends an express mandatory safeguard against involuntary denied boarding to another class of carriers.
impact_families.uncertainty: The operating carrier's agreement role and recital 7 support treating the wording as contextual shorthand.

impact_families.title: Czech cancellation conditions can preserve compensation despite qualifying rerouting
impact_families.effect: A passenger receives ten days’ cancellation notice and qualifying rerouting. Without extraordinary circumstances, Czech could require compensation that English excludes.
impact_families.rationale: The alternative eligibility conditions change access to the fixed Article 7 remedy and the carrier’s corresponding payment duty.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 12 and the provision’s structure support reconstructing the intended exception logic.

impact_families.title: Portuguese return-flight remedy lacks an express earliest-opportunity requirement
impact_families.effect: A passenger entitled to return to the first departure point could be offered a later flight under Portuguese despite an earlier available return expressly required by English.
impact_families.rationale: The omission can materially weaken the timing of the principal return-flight remedy. The reimbursement deadline does not replace that timing protection.
impact_families.uncertainty: The protective purpose could imply prompt return despite the missing express qualifier.

impact_families.title: French carriage priority expressly names guide dogs
impact_families.effect: A certified assistance dog that is not a guide dog could lack express carriage priority under a narrow French reading.
impact_families.rationale: The established difference concerns the dog's priority status. It does not itself establish exclusion from carriage or loss of the passenger's priority.
impact_families.uncertainty: Guide dogs may receive an inclusive contextual interpretation; no resulting refusal of carriage is established.

impact_families.title: Maltese may reverse the cancellation-compensation exceptions
impact_families.effect: For a cancellation without timely notice or qualifying re-routing, the positive Maltese condition could deny compensation otherwise due under English, assuming no extraordinary-circumstances defence.
impact_families.rationale: The connector governs access to the full Article 7 cancellation-compensation entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 12 strongly supports interpreting the listed circumstances as exceptions.

impact_families.title: Danish cancellation-accommodation trigger sets an upper time limit
impact_families.effect: After cancellation, a passenger outside Article 11 is rerouted two days later and needs overnight accommodation. Danish could exclude hotels and transfers that English requires.
impact_families.rationale: The reversed trigger could remove necessary overnight care during the wait for replacement transport, an important substantive entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 9 necessity conditions, recital 13 and the protective purpose support harmonization.

impact_families.title: Compensation exemption may require all possible preventive measures
impact_families.effect: Extraordinary circumstances could have been avoided through a possible but unreasonable measure. Latvian could require Article 7 compensation where English permits exemption.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed standard determines liability for the applicable EUR 250–600 cancellation-compensation entitlement under Articles 5 and 7.
impact_families.uncertainty: Possible measures could be interpreted as measures reasonably available to the carrier.

impact_families.title: Danish package-travel exception may also exclude the return flight
impact_families.effect: A package passenger with Directive reimbursement rights who needs to return to the first departure point could lose the separate return-flight entitlement against the carrier under this Regulation.
impact_families.rationale: The broader exception can remove an important return-transport remedy expressly preserved by English. The assessment does not assume that all remedies under the Directive disappear.
impact_families.uncertainty: Context may confine the exception to reimbursement; the Directive’s alternative remedies are not supplied.

impact_families.title: Special downgrade reimbursement may cover only one travel direction
impact_families.effect: A passenger downgraded on an intra-Community flight over 1500 kilometres from a French overseas department to European Member State territory could receive 50% rather than 75% reimbursement.
impact_families.rationale: The directional reading removes 25 percentage points of the ticket price from the statutory downgrade remedy, materially reducing that entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: Contextual interpretation could treat the route description as covering both directions.

impact_families.title: French hotel-transfer wording specifies the outward journey
impact_families.effect: A passenger receiving hotel accommodation could have to arrange the return transfer because the carrier treats the French obligation as covering only the outward journey.
impact_families.rationale: The supported change concerns one transfer within the care package; it does not remove accommodation or the underlying onward-transport rights.
impact_families.uncertainty: The care and onward-travel context supports interpreting the transfer obligation in both directions.

impact_families.title: Guide-dog certification may narrow priority carriage
impact_families.effect: Where limited capacity makes priority decisive, a certified service dog without guide-dog certification could lose the express carriage priority available under English.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed restriction materially changes eligibility for disability-related carriage priority, although the passenger's own priority remains and ordinary carriage is not prohibited.
impact_families.uncertainty: Guide-dog certification might receive a broader contextual interpretation.

impact_families.title: Hungarian cancellation exceptions include the exact arrival-delay limits
impact_families.effect: Following notice five days ahead, re-routing meeting the departure condition arrives exactly two hours late. Hungarian could exclude compensation while English preserves an entitlement absent another exemption.
impact_families.rationale: The inclusive endpoint can extinguish the principal cancellation-compensation remedy, including any amount that would remain after an applicable reduction.
impact_families.uncertainty: The scenario assumes the remaining exception conditions are met and no extraordinary-circumstances defence applies.

impact_families.title: Necessary measures may narrow the extraordinary-circumstances defence
impact_families.effect: A carrier could owe cancellation compensation because a necessary preventive measure existed, although that measure exceeded what could reasonably be required.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed threshold determines availability of an express defence to the principal cancellation-compensation duty.
impact_families.uncertainty: The recitals support interpreting necessary measures as reasonably necessary measures.

impact_families.title: Czech carriage priority expressly covers guide dogs rather than service dogs generally
impact_families.effect: A certified service dog other than a guide dog could lack express priority when accompanying a passenger with reduced mobility.
impact_families.rationale: The demonstrated consequence concerns the animal’s preferential carriage. Loss of the passenger’s priority, ordinary carriage or care is not established.
impact_families.uncertainty: The protective context could support a broader interpretation of the Czech dog category.

impact_families.title: Exactly three hours may prevent a compensation reduction
impact_families.effect: For an otherwise compensable EUR 400-category flight rerouted to arrive exactly three hours late, the strict Slovak reading could require EUR 400 instead of permitting EUR 200.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed boundary changes half of the statutory compensation remedy.
impact_families.uncertainty: The parallel two- and four-hour brackets support an inclusive three-hour ceiling.

impact_families.title: Spanish public notice excludes delays of exactly two hours
impact_families.effect: At exactly two hours’ delay, the prescribed Spanish display would not prompt the passenger to request the rights text, although the carrier must still provide an individual notice.
impact_families.rationale: The change affects the mandatory public message. Individual information and substantive assistance duties remain intact.
impact_families.uncertainty: Any practical informational effect depends on compliance with the separate individual-notice obligation.

impact_families.title: Finnish cancellation exceptions make departure and arrival limits alternatives
impact_families.effect: After notice five days ahead, re-routing departs at the original time but arrives five hours late. Meeting the departure safeguard alone could remove compensation under Finnish.
impact_families.rationale: The alternative connector can extinguish the Article 7 compensation entitlement despite failure of the arrival safeguard.
impact_families.uncertainty: The protective purpose and multilingual interpretation support requiring both timing safeguards.

impact_families.title: Permission to deny boarding may extend to non-operating carriers
impact_families.effect: A non-operating carrier arranging a journey could invoke Article 4(2) to refuse a reserved passenger carriage after insufficient volunteers came forward.
impact_families.rationale: The reading expands who may exercise an express permission to deny carriage against the passenger's will.
impact_families.uncertainty: Recital 7 and the operational context support limiting the permission to the operating carrier.

impact_families.title: Finnish increases downgrading reimbursement at exactly 3500 kilometres
impact_families.effect: A passenger is downgraded on a non-intra-Community flight of exactly 3500 kilometres. The reimbursement could be 75% of the ticket price rather than 50%.
impact_families.rationale: The difference increases the principal downgrading remedy by one quarter of the ticket price, a material change to the reimbursement entitlement.
impact_families.uncertainty: English's endpoint permits interpretation; no particular ticket price or actual loss is established.

impact_families.title: Reduced-mobility protection may cover additional causes
impact_families.effect: A passenger with reduced mobility from a non-disability cause who requires adapted services could qualify for priority carriage and care during delays of any length.
impact_families.rationale: The definition controls eligibility for important Article 11 carriage and care entitlements.
impact_families.uncertainty: A broad functional meaning of disability could harmonize eligibility.

impact_families.title: Swedish permits voucher payment with written consent without an express signature requirement
impact_families.effect: A passenger genuinely accepts vouchers in an unsigned written message. Swedish could permit payment on that basis, while English would require signed agreement.
impact_families.rationale: The supported consequence concerns consent formalities, including incorporated reimbursement methods. Genuine consent, prescribed amounts and protections against restricted rights remain required; imposed vouchers are not authorized.
impact_families.uncertainty: Interpretation of written consent and electronic signatures may reconcile particular cases.

impact_families.title: Delay accommodation may require a full elapsed day
impact_families.effect: A passenger meeting Article 6’s delay threshold, without Article 11 protection, could lose necessary hotel accommodation and transfers during an evening-to-morning delay shorter than 24 hours.
impact_families.rationale: The disputed trigger can eliminate the overnight-care entitlement. Article 9 does not expressly replace Article 6’s triggering condition.
impact_families.uncertainty: The necessary-night accommodation context strongly supports calendar-day interpretation.

impact_families.title: Hungarian delay-care trigger names the following day without expressly including later days
impact_families.effect: For a passenger outside Article 11's protected categories continuing the journey, an expected departure two days later could fall outside the Hungarian hotel-and-transfer trigger.
impact_families.rationale: The restrictive reading could remove necessary overnight care during a multi-day delay; the reimbursement option does not itself supply that care.
impact_families.uncertainty: Article 5's parallel wording and Article 9's multiple-night accommodation strongly support an inclusive reading.

impact_families.title: Italian re-routing choices expressly require an alternative flight
impact_families.effect: Comparable rail transport could reach the final destination before any replacement flight. An air-only reading could permit the carrier to decline that route.
impact_families.rationale: The restriction could materially narrow the core right to onward transport at the earliest opportunity.
impact_families.uncertainty: The aviation context supports a narrower reading of re-routing; the alternative must still provide comparable transport conditions.
